messages:
Ada: Heads-up — ran the multi-region chaos run and hit a tenant flip where region handoff caused p95 spikes and a bunch of KV cache misses. Any quick ideas?
Mike: Can you paste the proxy log snippet or the headers we used for routing?
Ada: log: `2026-03-22T15:20:30Z proxy: forward tenant=acme region=eu-west -> us-east latency=240ms kv_cache=MISS ttl=0` — happened during a control-plane swap.
Sara: If that tenant is EU-residency, forwarding writes is a legal no-no. We need a way to block or require explicit consent, not just blind forward.
Mike: Two immediate trade-offs: (1) Strict residency: fail requests in non-resident region -> higher errors but clear legal posture. (2) Best-effort forward with audit -> fewer client errors but cross-border data transfer risk and compliance work.
Leo: What about a consent token/header clients set after an admin flow? e.g., `X-Region-Consent: eu-west` — proxy only forwards when present.
Ada: Implementationwise we want zero sync control-plane lookup in the hot path. Proposed fast-path: proxy keeps per-tenant residency cache (local TTL), and logic: `if tenant.residency == LOCAL && !consent -> return 403` else forward.
Sara: I don't love forcing clients to change. Could we instead have the control-plane set a tenant-level `allow_forwarding` flag that proxies cache? That shifts burden to admin but avoids client changes.
Mike: Good option. Operationally: cache that flag with a short TTL (10s). On cache miss during a routing event, fallback options: a) route to resident and return `Retry-After: 1` to client, b) attempt forward + audit. Both have pros/cons.
Ada: Operator playbook sketch: 1) on eviction/cutover, probe local cache hydration, 2) if probe fails, mark tenant `degraded-local` and route only to resident, 3) if error rate >5% for 1m, auto-escalate pager.
Mike: Add hysteresis on ownership flips: require N consecutive healthy heartbeats (suggest 2s) before committing swap. Also introduce a `soft-forward` window (10s) post-flip where proxy can forward but must attach `X-Forwarded-Audit: true`.
Sara: Legal is tentatively OK with soft-forward if audits for forwarded writes are encrypted to an EU KMS and flagged as not to be used for cross-region analytics. Need explicit `forward_audit_destination=eu-kms` tenant flag.
Leo: Edge-case: streaming/chat sessions with large KV-state — forwarding means re-streaming tokens and can blow latency. Alternative: return an early `503` with header `X-Fallback-Region: eu-west` to prompt SDKs to re-open in resident region.
Ada: Good point. SDK can implement automatic reconnect when `X-Fallback-Region` is present. We'll need a brief SDK change to honor that.
Mike: For ergonomics add `X-Region-Prefer: fast|consent` so clients can indicate preference. `fast` lets proxy forward if it has cached `allow_forwarding`; `consent` forces explicit header.
Sara: I'll draft legal bullets to include in the RFC: who can toggle `allow_forwarding`, required audit retention, KMS scoping, and product opt-in guardrails.
Ada: Metrics: add `handoff_forward_rate`, `handoff_forward_failures`, `handoff_audit_bytes`, and `handoff_retries`. SLIs: p95 during handoff < 350ms and error rate bump < +2%.
Mike: I'll drive an RFC PR (diagram + header proto + runtime checklist + metrics) — taking it. ETA EOD tomorrow.
Ada: @Mike awesome. Can you also sketch the proxy cache behavior pseudocode? e.g.:
```
let cfg = tenant_cache.get(tenant_id)
if !cfg: // cache miss
  probe_controlplane_async(tenant_id)
  route_to_resident_w_retry_header()
else if cfg.residency == LOCAL && !cfg.allow_forwarding && !request.has_header("X-Region-Consent")
  return 403
else if cfg.allow_forwarding || request.has_header("X-Region-Consent")
  forward_with_audit()
```
Mike: That works. We'll need to ensure `probe_controlplane_async` is non-blocking and that the operator playbook can force-refresh cache for a tenant.
Sara: I'll add the compliance tests to the E2E test matrix (simulate forward, verify audit only stored in EU KMS, deny analytics exports).
Leo: Small SDK note: expose `onFallbackRegion(header)` callback so customers can implement reconnect logic.
Ada: Thanks all :thumbsup: — next step: Mike RFC PR, Sara legal bullets, I'll put operator playbook draft into the runbook repo.
Dev Bot: controlplane: swap finished at 1719991250, probes: 42 passed, 3 failed.
Mike: Noted the probe numbers. I'll include a short appendix about probe thresholds and a suggested default `cache_ttl=10s`, `soft_forward_window=10s`.
Ada: Cool. Follow-ups: add those metric names to infra-metrics, and add an alert `handoff_forward_rate > 20% && error_rate > 3%` to paging rules.
Sara: will do.
Ada: Thanks team — closing this checkin.
